title: A New Practice for a New Reality
coreMove: Spot overload as undefined open loops and move one live commitment into a trusted place with a next physical action.
sourcePressure: Modern knowledge work creates boundaryless overload because unfinished commitments stay mentally active as open loops until they are captured, clarified, and held in a trusted system.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Treating GTD as a calmer to-do list or generic stress advice instead of a specific handoff from memory to trusted external control.
sourceAnchorNote: The source sidecar contains no chapter-specific named people, named studies, or named places. Use only the listed GTD terms, official metadata, or supported artifacts; do not invent anecdotes.

sourceAnchors.name: mind like water
sourceAnchors.detail: Chapter 1 introduces this as appropriately responsive attention once loose commitments stop living in memory.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Mind like water is not a spa mood; it is what attention feels like after the next action is safely parked.

sourceAnchors.name: 2015 revised Penguin edition
sourceAnchors.detail: The official source bundle locks the revised and updated Penguin Books edition published March 17, 2015.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The 2015 revision matters because the overload is email-shaped and boundaryless, not only a paper-desk problem.

hook: stress is not about having too much to do
a messy desk proves the system is broken
counterintuition: the real problem is not time but attention
this is not about doing more but doing what matters
the simple move is actually the powerful one
tryThisNow: set a timer and write everything down
pick one task and make it specific
review your list and choose a priority
examples: timestamp plus name plus laptop plus decision repeated across all six examples
home kitchen clutter as mental-load shorthand

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person 'You' direct address, retrospective 'It took her three weeks to see', question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

exampleSpecs.domain: an immigration clinic paralegal clearing voicemail promises after intake night
exampleSpecs.audience: a paralegal with twenty-seven callers waiting for status updates
exampleSpecs.stakes: a missed document request could cost a client a filing window
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: The locked clinic door clicks behind Sarah before she empties every voicemail promise onto a legal pad, then circles the first call that needs a physical action.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a dark clinic hallway with the voicemail light blinking red
mustAvoid: turning the scene into general anxiety about helping people

exampleSpecs.domain: a municipal snow desk after an overnight storm
exampleSpecs.audience: an operations coordinator whose radio, email, and map all create commitments
exampleSpecs.stakes: a blocked ambulance route may stay unresolved because it is only in his head
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: At the dispatch console, James stops rereading the storm inbox and writes each live road promise into one capture sheet before choosing any route fix.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a wall map dotted with blue plow magnets
mustAvoid: making it about emergency heroics instead of capture

exampleSpecs.domain: a museum registrar handling loan forms during a donor reception
exampleSpecs.audience: an arts administrator whose precision work is interrupted by hallway requests
exampleSpecs.stakes: insurance dates and crate dimensions could drift across attention
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: "Can you also check the crate humidity?" makes Camille pause with the loan form half-signed and place the request into the intake tray before she answers.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a white cotton glove lying beside a half-signed loan form
mustAvoid: reusing a generic office inbox scene

exampleSpecs.domain: a bicycle courier managing repair notes and delivery promises during a wet shift
exampleSpecs.audience: a mobile worker who keeps commitments away from a desk
exampleSpecs.stakes: one forgotten brake repair note could turn into an unsafe morning route
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Rain beads on the cracked phone screen as Lukas records each loose promise before pedaling away from the repair shop.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: rain on a cracked phone screen
mustAvoid: bike helmet as repeated physical anchor

exampleSpecs.domain: a graduate lab coordinator after a freezer alarm weekend
exampleSpecs.audience: a research assistant with samples, emails, and faculty requests arriving together
exampleSpecs.stakes: a thawed sample or unlogged maintenance call could compromise a study
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: It took Aanya three failed searches to see that the real failure was not workload; no open loop had crossed into a trusted capture point.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a freezer alarm printout curled on the lab bench

exampleSpecs.domain: a neighborhood bakery owner before a holiday order rush
exampleSpecs.audience: a small-business owner whose commitments arrive from customers, suppliers, and staff
exampleSpecs.stakes: a wedding cake change could disappear into memory during the rush
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: What is actually making Marco tired: the number of orders, or the fact that three promised changes are still floating above the mixer?
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a flour-dusted order clipboard beside the mixer
mustAvoid: making the bakery about time management only

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm: a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'

skillTargets: diagnose open loops in concrete scenes
separate mental storage from trusted capture
choose next physical action over vague project labels

tryThisNowSpec: Write one nagging commitment on paper, add the first visible physical action, and name the place where that reminder will live.
